subject: Controlling legend order when inserting data points from a different data frame

messages.author: dd6646899d689f77
messages.subject: Controlling legend order when inserting data points from a different data frame
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to build a diagram containing a few reference points from a different data frame than my main one. A simplified example illustrating my issue is embedded below: I am plotting the data present in data frame a, but I want to insert a few data points from data frame b.

library(ggplot2)
a = data.frame(val=c(1,2,3,2,4,6),group=c('a','b','c','a','b','c'))
b = data.frame(val=c(2,3,4),group=c('d','e','f'))

a$group = factor(a$group,levels=c('b','f','a','e','d','c'))
b$group = factor(b$group,levels=c('b','f','a','e','d','c'))

p = ggplot(data=a,aes(val,val,color=group,group=group))
p = p + geom_point()
p = p + geom_point(data=b)
p

The problem is that this appears to cause ggplot2 to disregard the order of the factors when building the legend. I can understand that it wouldn't know what to do if data frame b introduced new levels not present in data frame a, but I would have expected that manually specifying all the levels in both data frames, even when they are not all present in either of them, would provide it with the information needed. It appears that this is not the case.

Is there any other way to make the legend entries appear in the order I want them to, rather than the forced alphabetic order they come out now?

parts:
Hi Sam,

Thanks, that did it. The problem was that my main dataset contains data from two time bins, whereas the points I was trying to insert contained data from only one of those bins, hence why I didn't initially think merging them would be feasible. But after some tweaking, I got it to work, so I'm a happy camper now!

Thanks,
Cesko

Op dinsdag 8 maart 2016 17:34:11 UTC+1 schreef Sam:

Hi Cesko,

I'm not entirely sure what you are after but would something like this work?

library(ggplot2)
a = data.frame(val=c(1,2,3,2,4,6),group=c('a','b','c','a','b','c'))
b = data.frame(val=c(2,3,4),group=c('d','e','f'))

ab <- bind_rows(a,b)
ab$group <- factor(ab$group,levels=c('b','f','a','e','d','c'))

p = ggplot(data=filter(ab),aes(val,val,color=group,group=group))
p = p + geom_point()
p

So bind them together into one dataframe? The order the factor levels.

HTH,

Sam
